subject: Staging warmup: SDK samples, rate limits & failover
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@paylance.com>, Elena Morris <elena@paylance.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Staging warmup: SDK samples, rate limits & failover

Hi Samir / Elena,

Great call this morning — thanks for walking us through the PayLance staging topology. Per our notes, I’m sending across a small bundle to accelerate the warmup: a short checklist, SDK examples (JS/Python), and a recommended client-side rate/failover pattern. I attached a placeholder for staging credentials (we'll share the real secret via SSO vault).

Quick recap / asks:
- Staging endpoint you gave: https://staging-api.paylance.com (we'll use a proxy to validate)
- Expected steady-state traffic for the warmup: ~25 rps, with load-test bursts up to ~100 rps for short windows
- Primary concerns you raised: graceful retries, avoiding double-billing on gen requests, and endpoint migration from your legacy /api/gen -> /v1/gen

Next steps I propose:
1) We set a 45–60m implementation kickoff (CS + Eng) to align on timeouts and rollout plan.
2) Monica (CS) and Vivek (implementations) will owner the runbook + smoke tests.
3) We iterate SDK snippet for token refresh and idempotency-key usage.

Attachments included (stubs):
- paylance-staging-credentials-placeholder.txt (placeholder only)
- warmup-checklist.md
- sample-snippets.zip (JS + Python quickstarts)

If you can confirm the staging creds flow (SSO or static token) and an initial target date for the kickoff, we’ll schedule.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

Company: Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Staging warmup: SDK samples, rate limits & failover

Thanks Aditya — useful summary.

A couple clarifications from our side:
- Staging auth: we can create a short-lived token for you (good for 72h) or you can use our SSO flow (preferred). For the kickoff, a 72h token is fine.
- Traffic: yes the 25rps steady / 100rps burst estimate is correct. We will run three load tests over the next two weeks (small -> medium -> large).
- Our main ask: ensure client-side retries are safe (no duplicate requests).

Best,
